name: Euronet Worldwide Inc
business: Runs ATM networks, prepaid and digital content distribution, and cross-border money transfer (Ria, Xe) for banks, retailers, and consumers worldwide.

events.what: Investor Day: new three-segment disclosure, digital accelerator revenue KPI, three-year outlook to 2028 including 100 to 200 bps of EBITDA margin expansion and 10% to 15% adjusted EPS CAGR
Closed acquisition of CoreCard Corporation (card issuing and processing platform); bolt-on, contributed $12.7M revenue from 2025-10-31 to 2025-12-31
Director Andrzej Olechowski died; board nominee count reduced. No CEO or CFO change found in the 8-K Item 5.02 sweep (2024-07-01 to 2026-10-02)

next_event.source: Investor Day already held 2026-05-20 (doc 49690); no further investor event found. Q3 2026 earnings are the next print (date not sourced).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is stated as 100 to 200 bps of EBITDA margin expansion over three years. The base year is read as FY2025 because the same outlook anchors the 10% to 15% EPS CAGR to $13.68 in 2028. Company adjusted EBITDA reconciles to VA EBITDA (Q3 2025 $245M call vs $244.6M VA).

statements.quote: With EBITDA growth outpacing revenue, we would expect to see EBITDA margins expand 100 to 200 basis points over the three-year period, with segment contributions following the revenue growth in similar pattern.
statements.speaker: Rick Weller

statements.quote: For 2026, we expect revenue of approximately $4.5 billion. We expect EBITDA of approximately $800 million.
statements.speaker: Rick Weller

statements.quote: Looking ahead, our outlook remains unchanged. As we discussed during our first quarter call and the Investor Day, our digital accelerators continue to perform well and are becoming a larger part of our business mix.
statements.speaker: Rick Weller
statements.doc_title: Euronet Worldwide Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year. Target = FY2025 VA EBITDA margin 17.53% plus 150 bps (midpoint of 100 to 200) = 19.03% in FY2028, vs FY2028 consensus 17.22% ($867.2M on $4,974.3M). Against the 100 bps low end the gap is 131 bps. Consensus FY2026 EBITDA of $758.5M is about 5% below the roughly $800M guided at Investor Day, so the street is already discounting the guide.

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin: Q4 2025 15.72% vs 15.83% (-11 bps); Q1 2026 12.52% vs 12.97% (-44 bps). Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $193M vs $206.2M a year earlier (Weller, doc 112124; revenue given only as '$1.1 billion', so the margin is not computed). Cross-border operating income fell 35% in Q2 on US immigration policy and a high-margin prior-year FX comparison. Margins are moving away from the target so far.

verdict: Cheap, with a numeric CFO margin target the street does not model, but this is a founder-run company with no leadership change; the catalyst is the same team's Investor Day, so it is not a GXO setup.
open_questions: Can EBITDA margin expand 100 to 200 bps by 2028 while cross-border remittance volumes (42% of revenue) face US immigration policy headwinds?
Why does FY2026 consensus EBITDA ($758.5M) sit about 5% below the roughly $800M Investor Day guide, and is the guide at risk at Q3?
Is there any succession plan for Mike Brown (CEO since 1996) that could become a leadership catalyst?
